title: fix(desktop): size and crop recordings from the frames the capture delivers
body:
## Problem

A Frame (area) recording plays back as a mostly black video with a piece of the selection in the top-left corner. Full-display recordings on a MacBook were affected too: they came out 2560×1440 and pillarboxed instead of the panel's 1.54 aspect.

## Root cause

`startEngine` sized everything from `screenTrack.getSettings()`. For desktop capture, Chromium reported the `maxWidth`/`maxHeight` ceiling the engine requests (7680×4320) instead of the delivered frames (3024×1964 on the owner's MacBook).

- The area crop scales the DIP rectangle by `trackSize / displaySize`. With 7680/1512 ≈ 5.08 instead of 2, the source rectangle landed about 5× too far and too large. `drawImage` clipped it to the real 3024×1964 frame, so only a corner was drawn and the rest of the canvas stayed black.
- Full display: `fitToCap(7680, 4320, 1440)` = 2560×1440, which is exactly the size of the owner's full-screen file `recording-2026-10-27-04-54-57.mp4`. That file is pillarboxed, because the compositor letterboxes the real 1.54 frames into a 16:9 canvas.

Evidence: `ffprobe` on the two takes from tonight gives 2650×1440 (Frame) and 2560×1440 (Screen), and the machine has a single 3024×1964 display. Both sizes follow from the 7680×4320 report and from no other input.

## Fix

`measureFrameSize` (new, `recording/frame-size.ts`) plays the track in a hidden `<video>` and reads `videoWidth`/`videoHeight`. Those are the frames the compositor's `drawImage` crops from. `getSettings()` remains as the fallback when the element cannot report a size.

## Verification

- Two new engine tests use a track that reports 7680×4320 while delivering 3024×1964. One covers an area crop and one a full display. Both fail without the fix and pass with it.
- `check-types` is clean, lint is clean, and the full suite passes (280 files, 2567 tests).

**Not verified:** I did not make a real recording with the fix. Please QA on the MacBook:

1. Make a Frame recording. The file should show only the selected area, filling the video.
2. Make a Screen recording. The file should be 1662×1080 or 2217×1440 depending on the quality preset, with no side bars.
